notes: Read all 19 source lines before editing. L1 `import { useEffect, useRef, useCallback } from 'react'` is preserved (reordered to `{ useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useRef }` for the native import-sort rule; `useMemo` added only to memoize the native companion handlers). L2/L5/L9/L17 blank lines and L19 closing brace carry over.

L3 signature `export function useInfiniteScroll(onLoadMore: () => void, hasMore: boolean)` ported verbatim — same name, params, and types; the returned `sentinelRef` (L18 `return sentinelRef`) is preserved byte-for-byte.

L4 `const sentinelRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)` -> `useRef<SentinelElement | null>(null)`. `HTMLDivElement` is a DOM-only type forbidden in native output (the native tsconfig omits the DOM lib), so a minimal local structural `SentinelElement` ({ readonly nodeType?: number }) stands in; a real DOM node is assignable to it under react-native-web, and the state name `sentinelRef` is unchanged.

L6-8 `handleObserver` useCallback ported 1:1: L7 `if (entries[0].isIntersecting && hasMore) onLoadMore()` is verbatim; L8 deps `[onLoadMore, hasMore]` unchanged. The DOM `IntersectionObserverEntry[]` param type is replaced by a local structural `IntersectionEntryLike[]` exposing only the `isIntersecting` member the hook reads, so no DOM lib leaks in.

L10-16 the useEffect is preserved with `[handleObserver]` deps (L16). L11 `const sentinel = sentinelRef.current` and L12 `if (!sentinel) return` are verbatim. L13 `new IntersectionObserver(handleObserver, { threshold: 0.1 })` is resolved through a `globalThis.IntersectionObserver` capability probe (`getIntersectionObserver`, the same idiom the useMediaQuery/useVehicleLive ports use for matchMedia/EventSource): on react-native-web-in-a-browser the real constructor is returned and used identically (`new Observer(handleObserver, { threshold: SCROLL_THRESHOLD })`, SCROLL_THRESHOLD = 0.1); L14 `observer.observe(sentinel)` and L15 `return () => observer.disconnect()` cleanup are preserved verbatim.

Browser-only fallback (contract #7): IntersectionObserver and HTMLDivElement do not exist on iOS/Android/Windows/macOS, so on real React Native `getIntersectionObserver()` returns null and the effect early-returns — an explicit, no-throw 'unavailable' state. To still deliver the SAME 'load more at the end while hasMore' behavior natively, a companion `useInfiniteScrollHandlers(onLoadMore, hasMore)` returns `{ onEndReached, onEndReachedThreshold }` for wiring onto a React Native FlatList/ScrollView; `onEndReached` applies the exact L7 rule (`if (hasMore) onLoadMore()`) and `onEndReachedThreshold` reuses the web 0.1 threshold so the 'fire near the end' intent is identical. This adds a native affordance without altering the original `useInfiniteScroll` contract.

Native-safety: no DOM modules, no `window`, no browser HTML elements, no Recharts/Leaflet/framer-motion, and no old web UI components are imported — only `react` (useCallback/useEffect/useMemo/useRef). The IntersectionObserver bridge is a runtime globalThis probe (mirroring the web `new IntersectionObserver` usage) typed against local structural interfaces, never a DOM import. No unit-suffixed fields (Mi/Min/Mph/Kwh/Kw/Psi), API paths, or i18n strings exist in this hook, so the SI cutover and i18n contracts are unaffected.

A focused Jest test (__tests__/UseInfiniteScrollParity.test.tsx) drives both paths via react-test-renderer with a fake globalThis.IntersectionObserver: verifies observe is called with threshold 0.1, onLoadMore fires on isIntersecting+hasMore, does NOT fire when hasMore is false or when not intersecting, disconnect runs on unmount, the hook is a safe no-op when no IntersectionObserver global exists (native), and the companion handlers fire/skip onLoadMore by hasMore with onEndReachedThreshold 0.1.
